bull.b: Sustained ~84% gross margins reflect strong pricing power and low incremental cost of goods for orphan therapies. This durable unit economics means each additional patient contributes high gross profit, supporting eventual operating leverage as SG&A and R&D are reduced.

A diversified global commercial footprint and established patient bases reduce single-market concentration and support predictable recurring product sales. Durable specialty distribution, payer relationships and multi-country reimbursement improve long-term revenue resilience.

Clear, near-term regulatory milestones create structural value optionality: approvals would materially expand addressable markets and shift the revenue mix toward durable, high-margin gene therapies. Successful filings also validate R&D strategy and de-risk future programs.

bear.b: Persistent ~-$497M TTM operating cash use signals structural negative cash generation that requires ongoing external funding or asset monetization. This constrains strategic flexibility, can dilute shareholders, and makes execution dependent on near-term financing or non‑operational receipts.

Negative equity and ~$1.2B debt materially weaken the balance sheet, limiting borrowing capacity and increasing vulnerability to adverse market conditions. Elevated leverage reduces headroom for strategic investments and raises refinancing and covenant risks over the medium term.

Management's path to profitability relies on monetizing Priority Review Vouchers and flawless commercial launches. These are binary or timing-sensitive events; delays, lower-than-modeled PRV proceeds, or launch setbacks would prolong cash needs and undermine the planned path to sustainable profitability.
